subject: Post-incident remediation & billing reconciliation for HelioMed (Sept 29 outage)
messages:
From: Anya Petrova <anya@heliomed.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Incident 2026-09-29 - request for SLA remedial credit

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick updates on the incident earlier today. We captured application-level retries across our worker fleet between 03:10 and 03:54 UTC on 2026-09-29. The outage caused a measurable degradation in request success rate for about 44 minutes; our telemetry shows increased latency and a backlog in the ingestion queue.

Per our contract we need confirmation about eligibility for a service credit and an estimate of the amount that will be issued against our September invoice. Please let us know:
- Whether this event qualifies under Redwood's SLA for September 2026
- The calculation you will use and the dollar amount expected
- How the credit will be applied (next invoice vs. standalone credit note) and expected timing

I've attached a CSV from our side with request drop timestamps and request ids (incident-log-20260929.csv). Procurement has asked us to get a formal credit notice for our records.

Appreciate a response within 48 hours so we can close our internal audit.

Regards,
Anya Petrova
Director, Platform Reliability
HelioMed

Attachments: incident-log-20260929.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrova <anya@heliomed.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-01T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Incident 2026-09-29 - request for SLA remedial credit

Hi Anya — thanks for sending over the logs and for the clear ask. I'm sorry HelioMed experienced this disruption. I've looped in our account lead (Marissa) and ops lead (Markus) so we can confirm the eligibility and get you a formal credit notice.

Action plan from us:
- Ops will validate our service telemetry against your CSV and calculate the eligible credit (target: within 48 hours).
- Marissa will prepare a formal credit notice and the proposed remedy (applied to next invoice, or standalone credit note depending on your preference).
- I'll follow up with a single reconciliation email with attachments and approval steps for finance.

Could you confirm the invoice amount you'd like us to reference for the September period (or confirm the invoice ID)? That will help speed the calculation.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

--
Attachments: none

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T15:30:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Incident 2026-09-29 - ops findings and recommended credit

Jonas / Olga — I reviewed our edge and serving telemetry for HelioMed for the reported window and correlated it with the CSV Anya shared. Summary of findings:

- Impact window: 2026-09-29 03:10:12 UTC to 2026-09-29 03:54:18 UTC (≈ 44 minutes)
- Root cause: regression in autoscaler health-check handling after a control-plane routing change; KV cache miss storms amplified latency during recovery. Fix rolled at 03:58 UTC and throttling removed at 04:02 UTC.
- Monthly uptime definition: Redwood SLA uses calendar-month uptime (total minutes in month). For September 2026 we compute a 30-day month (43,200 minutes).
- For HelioMed the downtime attributable to Redwood services in September = 44 minutes → observed uptime = (43,200 - 44) / 43,200 = 99.8979%

SLA tiers (Redwood standard customer SLA, excerpted):
- >= 99.95%: no credit
- >= 99.0% and < 99.95%: 10% credit of monthly invoice amount
- < 99.0%: 25% credit of monthly invoice amount

Given the computed uptime (≈ 99.898%), HelioMed falls into the 99.0%–99.95% bracket and is therefore eligible for a 10% credit.

Per our records the September invoice amount for HelioMed (MSA/committed spend used as base) is $32,000. Recommended credit amount: 10% * $32,000 = $3,200.

I've attached the ops incident timeline and a short root-cause summary. Recommend issuing a credit notice for $3,200 and applying it to the next invoice; if procurement prefers a standalone credit note (and PO reference), we can issue that instead.

Attachments: ops-incident-timeline-HelioMed-20260929.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

- Markus
Lead, Inference Operations

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T16:10:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Incident 2026-09-29 - ops findings and recommended credit

Thanks Markus — good write-up. Marissa, can you draft the formal customer-facing credit notice and include the calculation and how it will appear on their next invoice? Include the ops timeline PDF and the credit notice PDF in the package. Please also include the HubSpot ticket ID (HS-78452) and a DocuSign link for acceptance if procurement needs a signature.

Finance flow note: Per our process, we can either (A) apply the credit to the next invoice (fastest) or (B) issue a standalone credit note which procurement can tie to a PO. If they want a PO on the credit note, include the PO number in the DocuSign/credit template.

I'll prepare the outreach and propose: 1) immediate issuance of a $3,200 credit applied to October invoice, 2) standalone credit note available on request with PO reference.

Jonas

--
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aH-HelioMed-Incidents, HubSpot: HS-78452

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrova <anya@heliomed.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:02:00-04:00
Subject: Credit notice: Redwood service incident (Sept 29) — proposed remedy

Hi Anya,

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Attached is the formal credit notice and a brief timeline from our ops team. Summary:

- Event: partial service disruption on 2026-09-29 between ~03:10–03:54 UTC
- Determination: Redwood investigation confirms an internal service regression; HelioMed is eligible under the SLA for a remedial credit
- Calculation: per Redwood SLA tiering, HelioMed's observed monthly uptime places you in the 99.0–99.95% bracket → eligible for a 10% credit of the September monthly invoice
- Invoice referenced: September 2026 invoice (base amount referenced by account) = $32,000
- Credit issued: $3,200 (10% of invoice)
- Issuance options: we can (A) apply the $3,200 to your next invoice (Oct) automatically, or (B) issue a standalone credit note for procurement to attach to a PO. If you choose option B please provide the PO number and we will include it on the credit note and DocuSign the acknowledgment.

Attached: credit-notice-HelioMed-20261003.pdf (PDF, 5 pages) and ops timeline. Please reply to confirm which option you prefer and any PO reference. Once we have confirmation we will route the credit to finance for execution (expected completion within 5 business days after confirmation).

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your partnership — we're putting a follow-up set of mitigations in place to reduce recurrence.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: credit-notice-HelioMed-20261003.pdf (PDF, 5 pages)

From: Anya Petrova <anya@heliomed.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procure@heliomed.com
Date: 2026-10-04T11:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Credit notice: Redwood service incident (Sept 29) — proposed remedy

Marissa — thanks for the clear breakdown and for the ops timeline. HelioMed accepts the proposed remedy.

We'd like option B: please issue a standalone credit note and include our PO # PO-12345. Procurement requests the DocuSign acknowledgement for our records. Once we receive the credit note and DocuSign, we'll reconcile against the September invoice and process the PO for accounting.

Thanks to the team for the quick investigation. We'll keep an eye on the mitigation updates.

—Anya
Procurement (via procure@heliomed.com)

Attachments: po-12345.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
